ai.description: This slender skink reaches 12 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe and scattered black spots along its back. It features a translucent lower eyelid and smooth, glossy scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Riopa punctata* is the presence of a single, distinct dark spot on each scale of the body, forming clear longitudinal lines along the back.
ai.habitat: The Common Dotted Garden Skink inhabits leaf litter and loose soil in tropical deciduous forests, gardens, and scrublands across the Indian subcontinent, from plains to 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Common Dotted Garden Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and garden vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Riopa punctata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Riopa punctata* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to southern India, typically at elevations below 1,500 meters.
